newsitem.title: USA: CIA probing whether officer helped DNC donor.
newsitem.headline: CIA probing whether officer helped DNC donor.

text.p: The CIA is investigating whether a senior officer in the agency's elite clandestine service arranged for a favourable intelligence report on a major Democratic Party donor to be sent to the White House, the Washington Post reported Thursday.

Quoting unidentified government officials, the newspaper said the CIA's inspector general was examining if the now-retired officer, William Lofgren, was enlisted in the Democratic National Committee's effort to wangle White House invitations for Roger Tamraz, a wealthy Lebanese-American businessman with longstanding ties to the agency.

The Post said Lofgren was head of a CIA division that dealt with Russia and the republics of the former Soviet Union in late 1995 when the CIA passed information about Tamraz to a White House National Security Council member.

The NSC staff member was concerned about Tamraz's White House access because she feared he might be misrepresenting U.S. backing for one of his business projects. A top DNC official was trying to override her objection.
In December 1995, the NSC aide received an intelligence report on Tamraz, according to the newspaper. It added that the report had been requested by Lofgren.
Lofgren was just one focus of the CIA's inquiry into whether anyone at the agency tried to help Tamraz at the behest of the DNC, the Post said.
CIA officials have said it would be highly improper if the DNC were able to prevail upon the agency to do any kind of favour for a donor.
